label: <DEL> delimiter step (start of recall)
explanation: Fires at the <DEL> delimiter step (t == L, which outputs original token 0) in about 88% of sequences. 99.5% of the activation mass is on that step. Outside it there is only a weak tail: small activations on the last few original tokens just before <DEL> in longer sequences, and almost nothing in the copy phase. Activation is a little stronger in longer sequences. The top examples mostly have first token i/a and contain letters such as p, k, o, t, but these token effects are modest (about 1.1-1.6x lift). The delimiter steps where it stays silent (12%) skew toward short sequences (L=3,4). It does not fire on the first three steps or on copy steps after recall index 0.

issues: Core claims hold. phase==1 on test gives P 0.875, R 0.975, F1 0.922, mass recall 0.995. There is no activation at t=0..2. Copy phase gets 66 of about 2.7M steps, all at recall_idx 1. The original-phase tail holds 0.5% of the mass on orig_idx 4-8 (to_go<=3).

The claim that token effects are modest (1.1-1.6x lift) is wrong for the 12% of delimiter steps where the feature stays silent. Those silences come systematically from first token x length, not just length. Firing rate on the delimiter by first token: L=3: p 0.88, g 0.72, o 0.67, a 0.60, versus c 0.02, e 0.02, d 0.04, v 0.06. L=4: i 0.99, g 0.99, p 0.99, a 0.98, versus c 0.15, e 0.19, d 0.35, t 0.44, z 0.44. Even at L>=5: first_tok e 0.59, c 0.69, t 0.75, z 0.76, versus a/g/i/r 1.00 and p 0.999.
The length effect is real but steep, not a mild skew. Delimiter firing rate by L: L=3 0.26, L=4 0.66, L=5 0.89, L=6-9 0.92-0.95.

A first-token x length predicate closes part of the gap: phase==1 & ~((L<=4) & first_tok in {c,d,e,t,v,y,z}) & ~((L==3) & first_tok not in {a,g,o,p,r}). Test: P 0.909, R 0.957, F1 0.933 (vs 0.922). The gain is small because the silent steps are a small share of active steps, but it confirms the silences follow a systematic pattern rather than scattered noise.
The label itself does not overclaim. 'Delimiter step' is the right description of what the feature fires on, and only the explanation's description of when it stays silent is inaccurate.
skeptic.revised_label: <DEL> delimiter step (start of recall); silent mainly in short sequences (L=3,4) whose first token is c/e/d/t/v/y/z
skeptic.better_predicate: (phase == 1) & ~((L <= 4) & isin(first_tok, [tok(c) for c in 'cdetvyz'])) & ~((L == 3) & ~isin(first_tok, [tok(c) for c in 'agopr']))

final_label: <DEL> delimiter step (start of recall); silent mainly in short sequences (L=3,4) whose first token is c/e/d/t/v/y/z
